text:
The corpus-level comparison is available directly from `challenge_corpus`. It covers only entries with an accepted match: 86 Britannica documents vs. 84 Wikipedia documents (frequency cosine 0.5832). The words that most distinguish the Britannica vocabulary from the Wikipedia vocabulary are ranked by their z-score (higher = more Britannica-distinctive). Counts are total token counts across the matched corpus.

Words most distinctive to Britannica (vs. Wikipedia):

| Word | z-score | Britannica count | Wikipedia count |
|------|---------|------------------|-----------------|
| lime | 4.404 | 23 | 4 |
| abdomen | 4.368 | 21 | 2 |
| colour | 4.315 | 23 | 5 |
| platina | 4.233 | 18 | 0 |
| carbonate | 4.113 | 17 | 0 |
| instant | 3.625 | 15 | 2 |
| till | 3.513 | 15 | 3 |
| cells | 3.513 | 15 | 3 |
| eyes | 3.494 | 19 | 9 |
| letters | 3.386 | 21 | 14 |
| burnt | 3.371 | 14 | 3 |
| pipe | 3.349 | 16 | 6 |

For context, the words most distinctive to Wikipedia (lower z-scores) were century (0/302), roman (4/301), lightning (2/244), steam (4/253), erfurt (1/173), erigeron (1/173), city (6/245), fleabane (0/154), esarhaddon (1/168), william (15/354), coins (3/192), new (5/212).

Evidence: `challenge_corpus` (nemotron_challenge), corpus-level vocabulary comparison of all matched pairs; status ok; documents britannica=86, wikipedia=84; note: "Corpus counts cover only entries with an accepted match."

Caveats: The Britannica text is noisy OCR, so counts (especially for OCR-vulnerable terms like "platina" or "colour") may be affected by recognition errors. These are corpus-level aggregate counts, not per-entry breakdowns; I have not verified any individual entry text.
